text:
maria: Hey team — onboarding sample app (embed-bulk) is hitting a pile of 429s on first-run when we batch 64 docs. Repro on latest js-sdk.

kevin: ugh, seen that. Is it hitting per-minute token quota or concurrent request limits?

maria: looks like concurrency. We set maxConcurrency=16 in the sample app to speed up warmup. Logs show a burst of parallel requests and then a jittery retry storm.

sam: can you paste the client config?

maria: sure:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, maxConcurrency: 16, retry: { maxAttempts: 5 } });
await client.embeddings.bulkCreate({ inputs: docs });
```

kevin: hmm. JS SDK's internal backoff currently does fixed exponential with no jitter for bulk endpoints (we only added jitter for chat). That + immediate concurrency = synchronized retries.

leo: devx-bot: added test-case ticket #DX-827 for "bulk embeddings synchronized retry jitter" :eyes:
devx-bot: ticket DX-827 created and assigned to @kevin

kevin: thanks. I traced it quickly — two issues: (1) our client-side token accounting doesn't subtract estimated tokens per item when prefetching windows, so many requests get queued and then sent once CPU frees up. (2) retry-backoff math lacks full jitter for bulk endpoints so many clients retry in lockstep.

maria: that matches what I see: first 200ms we send 16 concurrent calls, then 1s later they all retry, and rate limiter on the edge starts returning 429 with Retry-After.

sam: is the edge returning Retry-After header consistently? If so we should honor it and not use internal backoff calculations.

maria: yes, edge returns Retry-After for most 429s. However, JS SDK currently ignores Retry-After for bulkCreate and falls back to internal backoff.

kevin: ok plan: small patch to sample app + SDK PRs
- sample app: lower default maxConcurrency to 6 and add adaptive window that observes immediate 429s
- SDK: implement per-endpoint honor of Retry-After and switch to full jittered backoff for bulk endpoints
- SDK: subtract estimateTokens(items) when acquiring concurrency slots so queuing doesn't cause bursts

leo: can we add an env var for onboarding to toggle this behavior so power users can still speed-run? maybe RW_ONBOARDING_FAST=true

maria: yep, I'll add that. Also adding a small CLI mode that runs a warmup with conservative defaults (concurrency 3, batch 16) so free-tier customers don't hit quotas during signup.

sam: For the SDK PR, also add a short e2e test that spins up a fake-rate-limit server to assert backoff honors Retry-After.

kevin: good call. I'll draft the SDK PR later today. Quick question: should we document this in devex docs or add a note to onboarding quickstart?

maria: both. Quickstart should have a "first-run warmup" section with recommended defaults. Devex docs should call out the difference between client-side concurrency and server token quotas and show adaptive patterns.

leo: tagging docs: @sam-docs (we can ping them once we have PR links).

maria: also, note for mobile sampleapp — the iOS SDK already enforced Retry-After for bulk but had a too-low semaphore, so behaviour differed across SDKs, which confuses users. We should aim parity: honor Retry-After + jitter + token-estimate semaphore.

kevin: agreed. Parity note: Android/Go/Node should match iOS behaviour. I'll make a checklist in DX-827.

maria: TL;DR — root cause: concurrency + no token accounting + no jitter + ignoring Retry-After -> synchronized retry storms on onboarding. Fixes: reduce onboarding defaults, implement jitter + honor Retry-After, estimate tokens at queue time.

sam: will follow up with a short sample app PR and a changelog entry.

maria: leaving the thread here. If anyone runs into the same while testing, post logs (sampleapp set DEBUG=sdk:throttle). :thumbsup:
